fair_value.method: Blend at a 12-month horizon of P/E (24x Oct-2027 NTM RemainCo EPS $7.60 = $182, 45%), EV/EBITDA (17x NTM EBITDA $638M less ~$175M net debt over 54.0M shares = $198, 35%) and a DCF (10.5% WACC, 3.5% terminal = $120, 20%), giving ~$175, about 4% below the $182.91 close.

5Y beta 1.71 (stockanalysis) x 5% ERP + 5.31% 10y (US Treasury par yield 2026-10-05; corrected by the citation audit from ~4.3%) = cost of equity ~13.9%; debt <5% of capital -> beta-implied WACC ~13%; 10.5% (judgment, unchanged) is generous. bear.story: AI capex growth stalls in 2028 (capex file low case) or the ~11%-of-sales technology customer defers or dual-sources; supply bottlenecks keep DC margins ~15%; corporate stays ~-$90M; FY28 EBITDA ~$420M; multiple de-rates to ~13x EBITDA / ~20x EPS.

base.story: DC +65% in FY27 and +30% in FY28 with margins back to ~20%, CHVAC +7%, corporate -$80M; FY28 EBITDA ~$580M, Oct-2027 NTM ~$640M at ~17x less ~$175M net debt -> roughly flat stock.

bull.story: Investor-day targets credible and the $4B LTA plus hyperscale order book convert: DC ~$2.9B in FY28 at 21%, FY28 EBITDA ~$720M, NTM ~$800M at ~19-20x (peer median).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$120 (EV ~$6.7B, ~11.5x FY28E EBITDA of $581M, ~17x FY28E EPS) the market would be pricing FY28 RemainCo EBITDA near $420M: DC growth stalling or margins stuck ~15%, most likely a deferred or lost hyperscale program (the ~11%-of-sales customer or the $4B LTA), a guide cut at the first standalone outlook or Investor Day, or an AI-capex down-cycle - not ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Valued only the post-spin Climate Solutions company. Round 2 re-verified the supervisor's findings in the filings: Q1 FY27 corporate was -$23.0M (consolidated adj. EBITDA $106.5M less DC $51.7M, CHVAC $41.6M, PT $36.2M), Jun-30 net debt $432.9M, Cash Distribution $155,991,275 used to prepay the JPM facility, the 10-K's ~11% customer and the 10-Q's $8.3M 5.8% notes. So corporate goes from -$60M to -$80M (-$21M FY28 EBITDA) and close net debt from $320-350M to ~$280M (~$175M at horizon). I stay ~9% below the DC '>85% earnings growth' guide after the 14.8% Q1 margin, which the supervisor accepts as defensible. FY28E EBITDA $581M, FY29E $694M, Oct-2027 NTM EPS $7.60. On a cleaner 10-peer set (median P/E 27.6x, EV/EBITDA ~19-20.5x), I use 24x and 17x (raised P/E from 22x after removing the double-counted horizon fade). That gives $182 and $198, and a DCF of $120 at 10.5% (5Y beta 1.71 supports the high WACC; weight cut to 20%). Blend $175, essentially unchanged from $174: lower net debt and a higher P/E offset higher corporate cost. My multiples now match the supervisor's (17x / 24x); I stay below its ~$204 because my NTM EBITDA is $638M rather than $675M (a slower DC ramp after the Q1 miss) and because I keep a 20%-weight DCF check. Skeptic findings: no short report, low leverage, covenant headroom; the bear case is execution, concentration and AI-capex cyclicality, plus uniform insider selling. The ladder is a 60/40 mix of a lognormal (median $178, sigma 0.55, below the spin- and crash-inflated 71% realized vol) and the scenarios (bear $105/25%, base $180/50%, bull $280/25%), giving a median ~$180. The right tail is slightly thinner than round 1. Research limits: 8-K/A not yet filed; peer forward EV/EBITDA is derived, not vendor consensus.
